items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: When he got mixed with Sushon, that all came up later, about the numbers that he had composed.

ctx.x: I have a record of Virginia Blues by the Louisiana Five in which they play the third strain of Skeleton Jangle as a part of the tune. It's signed, uh, Sincerely Yours, Don Fowler. Is there anything else you want to read?

You know, that's all. Not only the Louisiana Five, but everybody. It was a field lead from the all steel music and different things out the original Dixieland jazz band. Now they say these Negroes didn't hear these records. Joe heard them. If this man heard them, Joe Oliver heard them. Because Joe, in his thing, that's what he bases his rhythm on. Because he didn't know no better. He was just a Negro that didn't know no better. Like these even white crumbs who's supposed to be historians around New Orleans. They…

The letter here from... Let me see. I'll give you the full letterhead. It's a letter from Marshall W. Stearns. Yale Hot Club, 6th Linwood Place, New Haven, Connecticut. M. W. Stearns, President. Charter Unit of the UHCA. January the 11th, 1937, Mr. D.J. La Rocca, Earl Theater, Washington, D.C. Dear Nick, I have all your records from Liberty Stable Blues to the recent disc. I like the earlier ones better. Between you and me, our last argument should furnish you with plenty of publicity. I do think, however, that…
